title: UPDATE: AI Agent Rediscovers KVM VM Escape in 2 Hours
summary:
An automated cyber-security model identified an end-to-end path for breaking out of an isolated virtualization environment. Researcher 0x4d31 reported that the tool validated the exploit in approximately two hours after being given a single hint, demonstrating how adversarial models can autonomously replicate complex vulnerability discoveries usually reserved for human researchers.

The flaw is a zero-day in the Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) that allows a guest to gain root access to the host. Vercel confirmed the 'Critical' bug, which enables cross-tenant access on EC2 hosts, and paid its maximum $50,000 bounty to the original discoverer, Paulos Yibelo. As other firms now offer rewards of $200,000 for escapes from Firecracker or gVisor, industry experts warn that more than 1,000 recent kernel CVEs make current sandboxes vulnerable to capable agents.

fwiw, firecracker/kvm-style microVMs are everywhere, frontier labs use too

but only google with kvmctf, and vercel with sanbox challenge, which afaik actually put incentivies for researchers to break their production sandboxes.

this 0day is obviously extremely valuable outside these programs. but most researchers i know don’t want to sell bugs into some shady markets, they want to do interesting research, publish it, get credit, and do it legally.

need more programs like this, also dont be blind that your models will saturate every single bug
